A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACORD dataset and evaluation study despite the revised title. All 24 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and reranking evaluations, fine-tuning results, and query-expansion experiments in Table 3 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations, including model comparisons, fine-tuning results, and query-expansion experiments.

M1.justification: The annotation workflow, retrieval and reranking procedures, and fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. The rewritten labeling description and expanded annotation documentation do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 114 queries across nine clause categories and 126,659 query-clause ratings. The contract sources and evaluated short, medium, and long query scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain BM25, MiniLM models, OpenAI embeddings, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and the two Llama sizes. Newly cited clause-generation methods are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The query splits, top-100 reranking, metrics, and training grid are unchanged. The added NDCG score-conversion explanation repeats v1 Appendix C.5.1. Correcting one MiniLM bi-encoder size mention from 22.7M to 66M aligns it with v1's other description and Table D-3, rather than establishing a different evaluated model.

E4.justification: Fine-tuning comparisons, category breakdowns, pointwise versus pairwise reranking, and query-format experiments remain in Figure 2 and Appendices D–E. Removing the lexical-matching discussion does not remove these experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averaging for validation-based hyperparameter selection and the same 21% annotation disagreement rate. The description of tracking disagreements moves to Appendix A.3; no uncertainty reporting or statistical procedure is added.

E6.justification: Numerical benchmark results remain unchanged throughout Table 3 and Appendices D–E. However, v2 removes the explicit qualitative finding that MiniLM's bi-encoder performs much better than BM25 on the 'as-is clause' query and other queries. The BM25 results themselves remain in Table E-2.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 retains the same NDCG and normalized star-precision definitions and equations. The added explanation of zero-based relevance scores repeats an existing convention from Appendix C.5.1; no new mathematical result or reasoning is introduced.

C1.justification: The revised title, abstract, and conclusion emphasize clause retrieval, but retain the same contribution: an expert-annotated retrieval benchmark supporting contract drafting. Dataset scope and the claim of promising yet insufficient model performance are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explanation that BM25's failure to retrieve relevant clauses within the top 100 limits subsequent reranking. It also adds a footnote characterizing 21% annotation disagreement as common for difficult datasets and describing mitigation. Section 7's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 and gpt-4o-2024-08-06, and adds annotation-team counts of 12 attorneys and 10 students, student compensation of $20–35 per hour, and an estimated annotation valuation exceeding $1 million at stated market rates. Conversely, Appendix C.2 replaces the named ETH Zürich Ethics Commission with an anonymity placeholder.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds five works on clause recommendation and generation, including ClauseRec, and distinguishes ACORD from their smaller or simpler datasets. Choi et al. (2024) and Schwarcz et al. (2025) also expand the legal-LLM discussion. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title, abstract, introduction, and retrieval overview; reorganizes the labeling description into explicit steps; and adds Appendix A.3. These are localized rewrites and additions within the retained main-section and appendix structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1's typography changes, Figure 2 is vertically compressed, and Table 1's headings and caption are revised. Text and references reflow, but the figure and table inventory and their substantive displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The precise GPT model versions and expanded annotation-team documentation improve reproducibility and dataset transparency, while the added clause-generation literature improves positioning. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the lexical-failure explanation and named ethics-review body. The revision improves reporting without substantially changing the empirical evidence.
